instruction: Open the flight status page on the United Airlines website.

metadata.explanation: This variation asks the agent to navigate to the flight status page on United Airlines website. Similar to the original baggage fee calculator task, this is a straightforward navigation task. The evaluator checks if the active tab URL matches the pattern 'united.com/en/us/fly/flight-status'. No custom functions needed as we reuse the existing is_expected_url_pattern_match metric.

llm_judge_reasons: Evaluator logic correctly verifies the instruction requirement: The metric 'is_expected_url_pattern_match' checks if the active tab URL contains the pattern 'united.com/en/us/fly/flight-status', which correctly verifies that the user has navigated to the United Airlines flight status page.
Complete coverage: The evaluator checks the URL of the active tab, which is the only requirement in the instruction 'Open the flight status page on the United Airlines website.'

Getter can extract needed state: The getter 'active_tab_info' uses get_active_tab_info() which retrieves the active tab URL from the accessibility tree and returns a dict with 'url' field that the metric can process.

Metric comparison logic is correct: The metric uses re.search() to find the pattern in the URL, which will correctly match URLs like 'https://www.united.com/en/us/fly/flight-status' and similar variants.
Expected value is semantically correct: The pattern 'united.com/en/us/fly/flight-status' accurately identifies the United Airlines flight status page.
Data flow is correct: Getter extracts active tab URL → Metric searches for pattern in URL → Returns 1.0 if pattern found, 0.0 otherwise.
Runtime execution will work: The getter accesses the accessibility tree (available in the environment), and the metric performs simple regex matching, both of which will work at runtime.
